newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Sale of Pakhoed unit finalised.
newsitem.headline: Sale of Pakhoed unit finalised.

text.p: Dutch tank storage and shipping group Pakhoed NV said on Friday it had finalised the sale of its unit Furness to Hollandia Industriele Maatschappij NV.
As announced in August, Hollandia will pay 95 million guilders in cash for the unit.

Pakhoed has agreed to bear a net charge of 10 million guilders to restructure Furness' subsidiary Seaport Terminals. This has already been included in Pakhoed's 1996 first-half figures which were published in August.
Pakhoed will further provide a net contribution of 10 million guilders towards Furness' operating results, for which it will make a provision in the second half of this year.

As the Furness sale will be effective from January 1, 1996, Furness' first-half profit of three million guilders, which Pakhoed had already accounted in its own figures, will be taken as an extraordinary charge in the second half, Pakhoed said.
A 40 million guilders subordinated loan granted by Pakhoed to Furness previously will be continued and will be redeemed in five annual instalments.
Pakhoed will further handle a customs claim on Furness' subsidiary FIS.
The company said these arrangements should enable Furness to operate as an independent company with good prospects.
"Pakhoed will be able to fully concentrate on its core activities," it said.
